5	## 1. Definitions (fixed before the numbers)
6	
7	- **Unit / label / statistic** as the harness: a Foundation SETUP taken under the L1 (15:25) book; kept-vs-skipped difference of mean net (INR per unit); the session-matched random control percentile (`fz_report.random_control`, 2,000 draws); permutation p; block sign count. On a tape the statistic is computed by `harness.metrics` on a `harness.Table` built from the tape's own `features.parquet` / `trades.parquet` / `sessions.parquet` (`tapes.load_tape`, a copy of `harness.load` pointed at the tape folder). Every tape row is IS (the tapes carry IS calendar dates).
8	- **Three reference gates** (all as keep masks): `frozen_st7_st8` = keep where `fz_traded` (the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as it traded on that tape); `choch2_skip` = skip where `n_choch_since_bos >= 2` (mechanical reference gate 1); `sl_above_median_skip` = skip where `sl_dist_atr` > the tape's own IS median (mechanical reference gate 2). The two mechanical gates were **fixed in `tapes.py` before any tape was scored**; they are reference points for the engine-mechanics check, not candidates, and appear in no registration file (BRIEF H2 names the family `n_choch_since_bos >= k` without k; the stop-distance gate exists only here). Their ledger rows (section 3) carry the earlier wording 'pre-registered' in the config text, which this file supersedes. The engine-mechanics check: a gate on stop distance or CHoCH counts can read non-zero on a memory-free tape through the engine itself (Judge 2), so its null is not 0.
9	- **Generators** (fitted on IS bars only, `gen_tapes.py` docstring): *session bootstrap* (whole IS sessions with replacement, level chained through the drawn session's open-to-close path and a gap drawn from the IS gap distribution); *segment bootstrap* (30-bar clock-aligned blocks from random IS sessions, re-based and chained, same gap draw); *GMM-Markov* (GaussianMixture 4-6 full-covariance components by BIC on the z-scored per-bar vector (log return, log volume ratio to the clock median, range/atr14, close position), first-order Markov chain on the labels, per-session sampling with the clock volume profile, OHLC rebuilt consistently, samples clipped to the IS range per dimension). Full-length sessions only (375 / 75 bars); the real IS tape's short sessions are excluded from the pools (listed in `fit_<tf>.json`). Tapes are written in the near-month CSV format and pushed through `build/build.py --path` (engine.run with the Foundation rules, fz.run with the frozen ST7/ST8 block, L0 and L1 pricing, the same 261-column feature table).
10	- **Engine health of a tape / per-tape poor-null flag (repair round; `tapes.tape_health`)**: an IS session is *frozen* when the engine's protected level `prot` (bars.parquet) does not change inside it, equals the previous session's last value and no CHoCH occurs; a *dead run* is a run of frozen sessions longer than the real tape's longest such run (5minute 68, minute 69 sessions); *dead share* = sessions inside dead runs / sessions. A tape is **healthy** when dead share < 0.2 AND its SETUP rate is >= 0.333 x the real tape's. The flag reads bars / events / sessions / setups only, never a label or a gate statistic. **Tape sets**: `gates` = the **certificate**: the first DESIGN_N (20 / 8) healthy tapes per generator by seed index k (`tapes.tape_folders(tf, gen)` default; when the first build held fewer, the next seeds k = 20, 21, ... were generated until the count was reached: `run_tapes.py --target-healthy`); `gates_all_original` = the first build (k < DESIGN_N) with its locked tapes (the numbers the first version of this file reported); `gates_healthy_original` = the first build's healthy tapes only. The pass rule (section 7) reads the certificate set.
11	- **Null distribution** = per timeframe, generator, gate and tape set: p5 / p50 / p95 / mean / min / max of the tape diffs, the share of tapes with diff > 0, p50 / p95 of the control percentile, the real-tape value and its percentile among the tapes. **Comparison** (DESIGN_PANEL (c), Judge 1's go/no-go): the real-tape difference must be above the null-tape 95th percentile; here that is read on the two memory-free nulls (GMM-Markov and segment), with the session bootstrap as the stability read (share of tapes with the real diff's sign).
12	- **Reality check** per generator: within-session per-bar log-return std (bps) and excess kurtosis, autocorrelation of |r| at lags 1-5 (pairs inside a session), CHoCH / BOS / SETUP / L1-unit counts per session, the raw L1 book, the frozen gate's kept share, the final price level and median ATR14, over every tape built (the generator as it is) and over the certificate tapes; a generator whose median SETUP rate is outside [1/3, 3] x the real rate is flagged a poor null (generator level); the per-tape flag above is the tape level.
13	- **Adversarial validation (d)**: HistGradientBoostingClassifier IS-early (2021-10-01..2023-09-30) vs IS-late (2023-10-01..2025-12-31) on `harness.design(T)` of the real tape, IS rows; pooled out-of-fold AUC under `harness.purged_splits` (12 blocks, purge by exit bar, 3-session embargo); chance = 20 label permutations; variant A = all as-of columns, variant B = without time proxies (|Spearman rho| >= 0.9 with `session_idx`); SHAP (TreeExplainer) ranking on B with the direction of drift.

215	### 5c. Engine lock-out on the null tapes (repair round; `tape_health.csv`, `tapes/<tf>/<gen>_<k>/tape_health.json`)
216	
217	**Mechanism** (engine.py, protected level): the protected level `prot` is the last unbroken *candidate* swing of the current trend; a swing becomes a candidate only when it lies on the far side of the AVWAP anchored at the last trend flip (`qualifies`: a low below that AVWAP in an up-trend, a high above it in a down-trend). On a driftless random-walk tape a long one-directional walk leaves the anchored AVWAP far behind, no new swing qualifies, `prot` freezes at the last candidate, and a CHoCH (a close beyond `prot` against the trend) becomes unreachable while BOS (a break of the last swing high / low with the trend) continues at its normal rate; no CHoCH means no SETUP. The real market returns to its anchored levels often enough that the real tape's longest frozen run is 68 / 69 sessions (5minute / minute); the locked tapes carry runs of 99-932 sessions. A run can end when the walk wanders back (a recovered mid-tape lock-out; the tail rule alone misses these) or last to the end of the tape.

264	
265	## 11. Wording for REPORT.md (verbatim)
266	
267	> LLM hypotheses, round 0: sixteen skip rules were written from the user's words and the feature dictionary and hashed (sha256 `a3c5c06382227c95...`) at 03:29 on 2026-09-29. Labelled tables of the program existed from 02:49; the proposer states none was opened, so blindness is a process claim, not a data-ordering fact. Round 0's inputs also included FZ.md section 19 (ST7/ST8 comparator aggregates over the 2026 lab tape, which coincides with the OOS window; no Foundation outcome by read or hour), the one deviation from the judges' 'user's words + dictionary' rule. Scored on IS (L1): no rule and no union passes go/no-go; three rules (r0_m6, r0_m8, r0_f8) have no IS support because of a unit error in the session-range thresholds and are untestable; Holm-adjusted p = 1.0 for all sixteen; on 5 minutes the 'sideways' and 'retest' rules skip the better trades. Null result.

271	- IS only; nothing was read from OOS beyond row counts (the OOS rows are in the same parquet; only `T.is_mask` rows were ever passed to a statistic).
272	- Blindness of round 0 is the proposer's process claim (section 2); the labelled tables pre-date the hash by ~40 minutes; FZ.md 19 was read.

1	# FZ v3 design panel (2026-09-29)
2	
3	Three designers (quant-ML canon, sequence / representation learning, decision-making / RL) proposed studies for the FZ v3 program; two judges (feasibility-and-rigour, skeptical practitioner) scored each on feasible_here / rigour / expected_value (0-5) with keep = all three >= 3. Generated from the workflow result; the judges' fixes are part of the program. Feasibility was scored against the local 4-core box; in the cloud the compute ceilings do not apply, the rigour and overfitting fixes do.
4	
5	## Scoreboard
6	
7	| id | lens priority | J1 feas/rig/ev keep | J2 feas/rig/ev keep |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses | 1 | 5/3/3 KEEP | 5/3/3 KEEP |
10	| deep-sequence-regime-states | 2 | 4/4/2 drop | 4/4/3 KEEP |
11	| deep-sequence-rocket-probe | 3 | 3/3/2 drop | 3/4/2 drop |
12	| deep-sequence-vision-labels | 4 | 3/3/2 drop | 3/3/3 KEEP |
13	| deep-sequence-motif-shapelet | 5 | 4/3/1 drop | 4/4/2 drop |
14	| deep-sequence-pretrain-probe | 6 | 2/3/1 drop | 2/4/1 drop |
15	| quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo | 1 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/5/4 KEEP |
16	| quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate | 2 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/4 KEEP |
17	| quant-ml-canon-feature-importance | 3 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/3 KEEP |
18	| quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip | 4 | 5/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
19	| quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing | 5 | 5/3/2 drop | 5/4/2 drop |
20	| quant-ml-canon-regime-breaks | 6 | 4/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
21	| decision-making-1-fullinfo-bandit-policy-tree-gate | 1 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/4 KEEP |
22	| decision-making-2-exit-policy-fqi-exomdp | 2 | 2/4/3 drop | 3/4/3 KEEP |
23	| decision-making-3-robustness-resampling-multiplicity-adversarial | 3 | 4/4/3 KEEP | 3/4/3 KEEP |
24	| decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control | 4 | 5/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
25	| decision-making-5-kelly-bounded-sizing | 5 | 5/3/1 drop | 5/4/2 drop |
26	| decision-making-6-session-stop-rule-finite-horizon | 6 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/5/3 KEEP |
27	
28	## Judges' verdicts
29	
30	### Judge 1
31	
32	Skeptical-practitioner verdict. The tape sets the ceiling before any model runs: 1m Foundation is +1.9 pts per trade gross against ~16 pts of cost (mean net -922 INR, 15.2% winners, 4,502 IS SETUPs in 579 active sessions); 5m is 184 IS winners with the top decile carrying ~46% of gross and an IS-to-OOS mean shift from -277 to -1,060 per trade. So any gate must find a subset whose expectancy clears ~16-20 pts, and the whole signal lives in a few hundred trades on 1m and a few dozen on 5m. On that sample the block-bootstrap CI of a kept-vs-skipped difference will be several hundred INR per trade wide; most candidates will not clear it, and that is the honest expected outcome. Every library the 18 studies name is present (sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib) and statsmodels/torch/mapie are absent as assumed; feasibility failures are compute and memory, not imports.
33	
34	Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.
35	
36	Drop or defer eleven. The sequence and representation studies (rocket, pretrain, HMM/jump, motif/shapelet, vision) share one structural flaw: the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features the tabular studies already search, so they add trials to the ledger without adding a candidate, and the pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition; pretrain and 1m FQI also need 750-900 MB for hours on a box shared with another build. The two conformal studies and the two sizing studies do not change which SETUPs are taken: they choose a threshold on a score another study produces, or size a positive edge that does not yet exist; their useful pieces (slippage 3/5/8 sensitivity, Pareto front with user-chosen w, |net|-weighted coverage, one-lot-or-skip verdict) become sections of the gate study's deliverable. The regime-breaks study keeps only its break tests as the harness's pre-registration step (they decide time-decay weights and the OOS caveat); BSADF is a feature candidate for the importance pass, not a gate. The exit study is worth its parametric learner C (config keys the lab already has, 10 minutes by replay) but must be coordinated with the ST9-12 session, which already ran an exit grid on 2026.
37	
38	Two standing caveats every OOS table must carry: the OOS window (2026-01-01..09-25) is also the published lab dashboard window and was used by the ST9-12 exit grid, so it is not pristine; and the 5m Foundation label as built holds 358 of 1,012 trades past the entry session, so ST13/ST14 (square_off 15:25) must be judged on the recomputed intraday label and every comparator re-priced on it.
39	
40	### Judge 2
41	
42	Twelve of eighteen studies are worth running here; six are cut or folded. The binding facts: (1) sample size, not compute, is the limit: 684 IS winners on 1m and 184 on 5m, a 15-22% win rate, mean net -922 INR per trade against ~1,050 INR costs, so a gate must find a subset averaging > 16 pts, and the top-decile winners are half of gross wins; every learned number must therefore be reported as a CPCV path distribution (5th percentile), with |net| weights winsorised and kept-n floors. (2) memory: lab.py holds 1.24 GB and 759 MB is free, so the '2 processes under 1 GB' budget is currently one process under ~600 MB; the rocket probe at 10k kernels, the pretrain ladder, 1m FQI and 1m synthetic tapes do not fit until lab.py exits. (3) libraries: everything named that is present imports (numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, matplotlib, PIL, joblib); statsmodels, torch, mapie, hmmlearn, ruptures, arch are absent and every study that names them correctly hand-codes. Structural fixes that apply across the set: there must be ONE harness (merge quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's bootstrap/PBO): 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, one append-only ledger reached only through a score() function, PBO <= 0.2, kept-share/kept-n floors, slippage-8-pt survival, and ONE OOS script run once for at most 3 frozen candidates; all eighteen 'OOS once' clauses collapse into that, otherwise OOS is opened eighteen times. Four near-duplicate pairs merge: meta-label + policy-tree gate (the central study, EV 4), conformal-skip + conformal-risk-control (one operating-point step the user chooses on), the two sizing studies (conditional on a gate surviving; prior is 'one lot or skip'), the two harnesses. The L1 intraday (15:25) label written once is the only training label; the engine label's multi-session holds (358 of 1,012 on 5m) make purging by it too costly. Regime, novelty and state-model outputs enter as candidate features into the importance study rather than as separate gate searches, which is the cheapest cut in multiplicity. The LLM-hypothesis study needs a blind round 0 and a trials count equal to the labelled cells shown; the vision study runs as a 40-session pilot against mechanical proxies first; both must be separate agents from any study author. Cut: pretrain-probe (3-4 h, 750 MB, negative result foreseen), motif/shapelet (keep only the causal novelty score), rocket as proposed (reduce to a 5-minute ceiling check), both sizing studies as standalone. Run order: break tests and L1 label, harness, importance, merged gate, operating point, exit learners C and B (FQI on 5m only), session-stop, BOCPD/GMM regime, LLM rounds, vision pilot, null tapes on 5m; everything above 600 MB waits for lab.py.
43	
44	## Designers' rationales
45	
46	- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.
47	
48	Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).
49	
50	Machine: 4 cores, 7.9 GB total but only ~0.9 GB free at the time of writing (lab.py rebuild holds 1.5 GB, the 1m feature build ~200 MB), so studies must run one at a time until the rebuild finishes, and every study is designed to peak under 800 MB with 1m windows stored as float32 and never more than ~150k pretraining windows in memory at once.
51	
52	Common protocol shared by all six (each study's leakage_controls field adds the study-specific parts): (1) unit = Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade from the build (fnd_net_inr, fnd_win, exit reason); (2) every feature/window uses bars <= setup_i (the SETUP bar's close is the entry; the window ends at k inclusive); (3) IS-only learning with purged, embargoed, session-blocked CV: 5 contiguous chronological blocks of ~205 IS sessions, training SETUPs whose Foundation exit session falls in the test block or its embargo are purged, embargo = max sessions_held observed on that timeframe (+1), all normalisation/PCA/kernel-bias/model parameters fit inside the training folds; (4) OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) is scored once by a single logged script run with the model frozen on all IS, never re-tuned; (5) judgement is kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference with fz_report.permutation_p, the session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control; the current ST7/ST8 sit at the 39.6th/57th percentile, so the bar is 'above the 95th'), precision/recall on losers, and the share of top-decile winners skipped; net alone is never the criterion because every gate that trades less banks ~1,114 INR per skipped 1m trade; (6) multiplicity: every configuration tried is counted and a max-T permutation across the family (White's Reality Check style) is reported next to the single-rule p; (7) output = a candidate ST13/ST14 gate block: <= 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3 over named as-of features with provenance 'learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha'; any non-scalar artefact (HMM parameters, a shapelet template) is offered only as an alternative that needs a user decision on a new fz key and code contract.
53	
54	Ordering: the LLM-hypothesis study is first because it is config-native, cheap and directly encodes the user's own reads; the regime-state study second because 'sideways hurts' is the user's central claim and the models are small enough to ship; the random-kernel probe third as the cheapest ceiling test for 'is there information in the bar shape at all'; vision labels fourth because they give the user's visual notion of sideways a ground truth (and the first number, Foundation expectancy by hindsight label, decides whether any causal detector is worth building); motif/shapelet fifth; self-supervised pretraining last because without a framework it is the most likely to report 'nothing beyond PCA'. Sizing and exits: studies 2 and 3 emit a per-SETUP expectancy score; the brief's exits stay Foundation's, so sizing appears only as a secondary output (lots 0/1/2 by score tercile) judged with the same control; a during-trade version of the window models for early exits is a natural follow-on once the position-path table exists, and is not proposed here.
55	
56	- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (uniqueness is 1 by construction for Foundation labels; only the triple-barrier variants with vertical barriers overlap and those get the concurrency weights inside study 1); HRP / portfolio construction (one instrument); deep sequence models and transformers (1k-5k labels, no GPU, and nothing to distil into 8 rules); sequential RL (one-step decision with the counterfactual observed); generative AI in the LLM sense (no standing in the canon at this sample size; the only generative element the canon endorses here is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions in study 2, which is what gives the confidence intervals). OOS discipline shared by all six: candidate configs and the exact scoring scripts are frozen to JSON with a sha before any OOS row is read; the harness pre-registers the go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0, deflated-Sharpe p < 0.1, at most three candidates across all lenses get the one OOS look); the frozen ST7/ST8 gate is always one of the comparators; ST13/ST14 must carry square_off "15:25" so that the traded book matches the label the gate was learned on.
57	
58	- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.
59	
60	## Studies
61	
62	### deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses (priority 1)
63	
64	**technique.** LLM-as-hypothesis-generator with pre-registration and a family-wise permutation test: Claude reads IS-only summaries of the per-SETUP feature table and writes a fixed, hashed list of candidate skip rules before any rule is scored.
65	
66	**what_it_answers.** Does a small set of human-readable rules, written from the user's own observations (sideways after repeated CHoCH, reaction to visibly high volume, respected vs broken levels, time of day, room read) plus what the IS marginals show, skip losers without skipping winners; and is the effect real after correcting for having proposed several rules at once? This is the only study whose raw output is already in ST13/ST14 config form.
67

Step 2, proposal: Claude writes deep_llm_rules_round1.json with <= 8 rules, each a conjunction of <= 3 comparisons on named features (e.g. {n_choch_since_bos >= 2, bars_since_bos > 36, range36_atr < 1.5} -> skip), with the reason in the user's words; the file's sha256 and timestamp are logged (deep_llm_register.txt) before step 3 runs. Step 3, scoring (deep_llm_eval.py): each rule on 5-fold purged session-blocked IS CV: kept n, skipped n, mean net kept vs skipped, permutation p (fz_report.permutation_p with 2,000 draws), losers-recall / precision, share of top-decile winners skipped, and the session-matched control percentile of the kept set; then a max-T permutation across all rules in the round (the family-wise p for the best rule), and Holm-adjusted single p's. Step 4: rules with Holm p < 0.05 and control percentile >= 95 on CV are combined greedily (order by CV kept-vs-skipped gain, stop when the marginal rule's gain < 200 INR/trade or when winners skipped rises) into a rule list of <= 8; a second round is allowed only if it is registered as round 2 and the multiplicity count carries over. Step 5: the frozen list scored once on OOS with the same table. Nature 2024, for LLM-proposed heuristics scored by a fixed evaluator), disciplined by pre-registration (Nosek et al. 2018) against the garden of forking paths (Gelman & Loken 2013) and by the finance-native family-wise tests for data-snooped trading rules (White 2000 Reality Check; Hansen 2005 SPA; Westfall & Young max-T).

346	## 8. Caveats and what would falsify these nulls
347	
348	- The tapes' price level follows a random walk of drawn sessions and gaps: over 1,026 sessions some tapes end far from the real level (see `close_last` in section 5); the engine is scale-free (checked: x2 prices give identical event counts), but INR differences scale with the level, so a high-level tape widens the null in INR. This makes the p95 conservative (harder to beat); an ATR-normalised statistic would be tighter and is not the registered one.
349	- The GMM-Markov tape's return kurtosis is below the real tape's (a 6-component mixture cannot carry a kurtosis of ~25) and its |r| autocorrelation dies within a few bars; Judge 1's warning (a narrower-than-reality null over-rejects) is why the segment bootstrap is read alongside it and the pass rule needs both.
350	- The session bootstrap keeps every within-session dependence, so it is a stability read, not a null: a gate that works within the day should keep its sign there.
351	- Engine lock-out (section 5c, measured): on the first build the engine's protected level froze and the CHoCH stream stopped for 22-91% of the sessions on 5minute: GMM-Markov 6/20, segment bootstrap (30-bar blocks) 4/20, session bootstrap 10/20; minute: GMM-Markov 0/8, segment bootstrap (30-bar blocks) 1/8, session bootstrap 1/8 tapes (frozen-run rule; the refuters' tail rule finds 12 of 84), while BOS continued at the normal rate; the locked tapes carry as few as 78 L1 units (5minute) against 770-1211 on the certificate tapes; 430 L1 units (minute) against 613-1650 on the certificate tapes. The certificate (section 4) excludes them and was topped up to the design count with the next seeds; the first-build numbers with and without them are in section 4a (verdicts unchanged). The lock-out is itself a property of a memory-free tape (the real market returns to its anchored levels; a random walk need not), so the healthy set is conditioned on 'the engine ran', not on any gate statistic.

353	- The 1-minute tapes are one trading year (247 IS sessions) with 8 tapes per generator: their null percentiles rest on 8 values and are wider than the 5-minute ones; the 5-minute nulls are the primary certificate, as both judges asked.

161	def welch_t(net, fires):
162	    """Two-sided Welch t of kept (not fired) vs skipped (fired) mean net; NaN when either side has < 2 rows."""
163	    k, s = net[~fires], net[fires]
164	    if len(k) < 2 or len(s) < 2: return np.nan
165	    return float((k.mean() - s.mean()) / np.sqrt(k.var(ddof=1) / len(k) + s.var(ddof=1) / len(s)))

168	def max_t(net, R, tag, draws=MAXT_DRAWS):
169	    """Westfall-Young max-T over the rules (rows of R = fired masks): permute net across rows, recompute every rule's |t|, take the
170	    max. Returns the observed t per rule, the family-wise p of the best rule and the step-down adjusted p per rule. Rules with an
171	    undefined t (skipped_n <= 1) are excluded from the max but keep their place in the family (adjusted p = 1)."""
172	    n = len(net); M = R.shape[0]
173	    obs = np.array([welch_t(net, R[j]) for j in range(M)])
174	    ok = np.isfinite(obs)
175	    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(hashlib.sha1(f"fz|llm_hypotheses|maxT|{tag}".encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % (2 ** 32))
176	    Rk = (~R[ok]).astype(float); Rs = R[ok].astype(float)
177	    nk, ns = Rk.sum(axis=1), Rs.sum(axis=1)
178	    T_perm = np.empty((draws, int(ok.sum())))
179	    for d in range(draws):
180	        p = net[rng.permutation(n)]
181	        sk, ss = Rk @ p, Rs @ p; qk, qs = Rk @ (p * p), Rs @ (p * p)
182	        mk, ms = sk / nk, ss / ns
183	        vk = (qk - nk * mk * mk) / (nk - 1); vs = (qs - ns * ms * ms) / (ns - 1)
184	        T_perm[d] = (mk - ms) / np.sqrt(vk / nk + vs / ns)
185	    A = np.abs(T_perm); a_obs = np.abs(obs[ok])
186	    best = int(np.argmax(a_obs)); fw_p = float((1 + (A.max(axis=1) >= a_obs[best] - 1e-12).sum()) / (1 + draws))
187	    # step-down: order rules by |t| descending; adjusted p_i = P(max over rules ranked i.. of |t*| >= |t_i|), monotone
188	    order = np.argsort(-a_obs); adj = np.empty(len(a_obs))
189	    prev = 0.0
190	    for i, j in enumerate(order):
191	        sub = A[:, order[i:]].max(axis=1)
192	        p = float((1 + (sub >= a_obs[j] - 1e-12).sum()) / (1 + draws)); prev = max(prev, p); adj[j] = prev
193	    adj_all = np.ones(M); adj_all[ok] = adj
194	    ids_ok = np.flatnonzero(ok)
195	    return dict(draws=draws, statistic="two-sided Welch t of kept vs skipped mean net, net permuted across IS rows",
196	                t_obs=[None if not np.isfinite(x) else round(float(x), 3) for x in obs], best_rule_index=int(ids_ok[best]),
197	                best_abs_t=round(float(a_obs[best]), 3), familywise_p_best=round(fw_p, 4),
198	                maxt_null_p95=round(float(np.quantile(A.max(axis=1), 0.95)), 3), adjusted_p=[round(float(x), 4) for x in adj_all],
199	                rules_in_family=M, rules_testable=int(ok.sum()))

202	def holm(p):
203	    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float); m = len(p); order = np.argsort(p); out = np.empty(m); prev = 0.0
204	    for i, j in enumerate(order):
205	        v = min(1.0, (m - i) * p[j]); prev = max(prev, v); out[j] = prev
206	    return out

264	    vec_u = H.session_vectors(T, ~U, rows); boot_u = H.bootstrap_ci(vec_u, tag=f"{tf}|union")
265	    log(f"[{tf}] union  skipped {res_u['skipped_n']} kept {res_u['kept_n']} diff {res_u['diff']} ctrl {res_u['control_pct']} perm_p {res_u['perm_p']} loserR {res_u['loser_recall']} winR(w) {res_u['winner_recall_weighted']} | L0 diff {res_u0['diff']} ctrl {res_u0['control_pct']}")
266	    # multiplicity
267	    mt = max_t(T.net[rows], R[:, rows], tag=f"{tf}|L1")
268	    fam_vecs = vecs + [vec_u]
269	    pbo_diff, pbo_km = H.pbo(fam_vecs, "diff"), H.pbo(fam_vecs, "kept_mean")
270	    spa_ = H.spa(fam_vecs, tag=f"{tf}|llm_round0"); eff = H.effective_trials(fam_vecs)
271	    srs = []
272	    for v in fam_vecs:
273	        x = kept_session_series(v); srs.append(float(x.mean() / x.std(ddof=1)) if len(x) > 2 and x.std(ddof=1) > 0 else np.nan)
274	    sr_var = float(np.nanvar(np.array(srs), ddof=1)) if np.isfinite(srs).sum() > 1 else None
275	    dsrs = [H.deflated_sharpe(kept_session_series(v), N_TRIALS_ROUND, sr_var if sr_var and sr_var > 0 else None) for v in fam_vecs]
276	    log(f"[{tf}] max-T: best |t| {mt['best_abs_t']} (rule {rules[mt['best_rule_index']]['id']}), family-wise p {mt['familywise_p_best']}, null 95th pct of max|t| {mt['maxt_null_p95']}; PBO(diff) {pbo_diff['pbo']} PBO(kept_mean) {pbo_km['pbo']}; SPA p {spa_['spa_p']} (RC p {spa_['rc_p']}); effective trials {eff}")
277	    # go / no-go per rule and for the union (no cpcv item: a fixed rule has no fitted threshold)
278	    gng = {}
279	    for j, p in enumerate(per):
280	        ok, ch = H.go_no_go(p["L1"], tf, cpcv=None, pbo_value=pbo_diff["pbo"], dsr=dsrs[j], spa_p=spa_["spa_p"], boot=p["boot"]) if not p["untestable"] else (False, {"untestable": (False, "no IS support")})
281	        p["go_no_go"] = dict(passed=bool(ok), checks={k: [bool(v[0]), v[1]] for k, v in ch.items()}, cpcv="not applicable: fixed rule, no fitted threshold"); p["dsr"] = dsrs[j]
282	        p["maxt_t"] = mt["t_obs"][j]; p["maxt_adjusted_p"] = mt["adjusted_p"][j]; gng[p["id"]] = bool(ok)
283	    ok_u, ch_u = H.go_no_go(res_u, tf, cpcv=None, pbo_value=pbo_diff["pbo"], dsr=dsrs[-1], spa_p=spa_["spa_p"], boot=boot_u)
284	    union = dict(L1=res_u, L0=res_u0, boot=boot_u, blocks=block_table(T, U, rows), dsr=dsrs[-1],
285	                 go_no_go=dict(passed=bool(ok_u), checks={k: [bool(v[0]), v[1]] for k, v in ch_u.items()}, cpcv="not applicable: fixed rule list, no fitted threshold"))
286	    log(f"[{tf}] go/no-go: " + ", ".join(f"{k} {'PASS' if v else 'fail'}" for k, v in gng.items()) + f", union {'PASS' if ok_u else 'fail'}")
287	    results["timeframes"][tf] = dict(n_is_L1=int(T.is_mask.sum()), n_is_L0=int(T0.is_mask.sum()), all_mean_L1=round(float(T.net[rows].mean()), 2), all_mean_L0=round(float(T0.net[rows0].mean()), 2),
288	                                     rules=per, union=union, max_t=mt, pbo_diff=pbo_diff, pbo_kept_mean=pbo_km, spa=spa_, effective_trials=eff,
289	                                     sharpe_family=[None if not np.isfinite(s) else round(s, 4) for s in srs], sharpe_var_family=sr_var,
290	                                     support=sup, runtime_s=round(time.time() - t0, 1))
291	    return T, R, per, res_u
292	
293	
294	def combination(tf, T, R, per, rules, results):
295	    """Design step 4 (pre-specified): rules with Holm p < 0.05 (m = 16 over the round) and control pct >= 95, greedily combined in
296	    order of diff; stop when the marginal diff < 200 INR/trade or the |net|-weighted winner recall falls. Every step is a ledger row."""
297	    rows = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
298	    elig = [j for j, p in enumerate(per) if not p["untestable"] and p["holm_p_round"] < COMBO_HOLM_ALPHA and (p["L1"]["control_pct"] or 0) >= COMBO_CONTROL_MIN]
299	    out = dict(eligible=[per[j]["id"] for j in elig], steps=[], final=None,
300	               rule=f"Holm p (m={HOLM_M}) < {COMBO_HOLM_ALPHA} and control pct >= {COMBO_CONTROL_MIN}; greedy by diff; stop when marginal diff < {COMBO_MIN_GAIN} or |net|-weighted winner recall falls")
301	    if not elig:
302	        out["final"] = "no rule qualifies; no combination scored"; log(f"[{tf}] combination: no rule qualifies"); results["timeframes"][tf]["combination"] = out; return
303	    elig.sort(key=lambda j: -(per[j]["L1"]["diff"] or -1e9))
304	    chosen, cur, prev_res = [], np.zeros(T.n, dtype=bool), None
305	    for j in elig:
306	        cand = cur | R[j]; cfg = dict(round=0, rule="combo", members=[per[i]["id"] for i in chosen + [j]], then="skip", sha256_rules=REGISTERED_SHA[:16])
307	        res = H.score(T, ~cand, FAMILY_COMBO, cfg, script=__file__, note=NOTE)
308	        step = dict(added=per[j]["id"], id=res["id"], kept_n=res["kept_n"], diff=res["diff"], control_pct=res["control_pct"], winner_recall_weighted=res["winner_recall_weighted"])
309	        if prev_res is not None:
310	            marginal = (res["diff"] or 0) - (prev_res["diff"] or 0)
311	            step["marginal_diff"] = round(marginal, 2)
312	            if marginal < COMBO_MIN_GAIN or (res["winner_recall_weighted"] or 0) < (prev_res["winner_recall_weighted"] or 0):
313	                step["accepted"] = False; out["steps"].append(step); log(f"[{tf}] combination: stop before {per[j]['id']} (marginal {marginal:.1f})"); break
314	        step["accepted"] = True; out["steps"].append(step); chosen.append(j); cur = cand; prev_res = res
315	        log(f"[{tf}] combination: + {per[j]['id']} -> kept {res['kept_n']} diff {res['diff']} ctrl {res['control_pct']}")
316	    out["final"] = dict(members=[per[i]["id"] for i in chosen], ledger_id=prev_res["id"] if prev_res else None, L1=prev_res)
317	    results["timeframes"][tf]["combination"] = out
318	
319	
320	def main():
321	    t0 = time.time()
322	    log(f"=== score_round0.py {D.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')} (repair round) ===")
323	    sha, appended = registration()
324	    rules_all = json.load(open(RULES, encoding="utf-8"))
325	    results = dict(study="llm_hypotheses", round_scored=0, scored_at=D.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), rules_sha256=sha,
326	                   registration_correction_appended=appended, ledger_sha_before=H.ledger_sha(), family=FAMILY, family_combo=FAMILY_COMBO, note=NOTE,
327	                   label_primary="L1", label_robustness="L0", split="IS", holm_m=HOLM_M, n_trials_round=N_TRIALS_ROUND, maxt_draws=MAXT_DRAWS, timeframes={})
328	    keep = {}
329	    for tf in TFS: keep[tf] = run_tf(tf, rules_all, results)
330	    # Holm over the 16 rules of the round (both timeframes; an untestable rule enters with p = 1)
331	    allp, index = [], []
332	    for tf in TFS:
333	        for j, p in enumerate(results["timeframes"][tf]["rules"]):
334	            pp = p["L1"]["perm_p"]; allp.append(1.0 if pp is None else float(pp)); index.append((tf, j))
335	    hp = holm(allp)
336	    for (tf, j), v in zip(index, hp): results["timeframes"][tf]["rules"][j]["holm_p_round"] = round(float(v), 4)
337	    results["holm"] = dict(m=HOLM_M, raw_p=[round(x, 4) for x in allp], holm_p=[round(float(x), 4) for x in hp], min_holm_p=round(float(hp.min()), 4),
338	                           rules=[f"{tf}:{results['timeframes'][tf]['rules'][j]['id']}" for tf, j in index])
339	    log(f"Holm over the {len(allp)} rules of round 0: min adjusted p {hp.min():.4f}")
340	    for tf in TFS:
341	        T, R, per, _ = keep[tf]; combination(tf, T, R, per, rules_all[tf], results)
342	    results["ledger_sha_after"] = H.ledger_sha()
343	    results["ledger_rows"] = dict(round0=len(H.read_ledger(FAMILY)), combo=len(H.read_ledger(FAMILY_COMBO)))
344	    results["null_result"] = not any(p["go_no_go"]["passed"] for tf in TFS for p in results["timeframes"][tf]["rules"]) and not any(results["timeframes"][tf]["union"]["go_no_go"]["passed"] for tf in TFS)
345	    results["runtime_s"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
346	    json.dump(results, open(os.path.join(HERE, "round0_results.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1, default=lambda z: z.item() if hasattr(z, "item") else str(z))
347	    # flat CSVs
348	    keys = ["n", "kept_n", "skipped_n", "kept_share", "kept_mean", "skipped_mean", "diff", "diff_top1_removed", "perm_p", "control_pct", "loser_recall", "loser_precision",
349	            "winner_recall", "winner_recall_weighted", "top_decile_winners_skipped", "kept_mean_slip8", "sign_blocks", "kept_pf"]
350	    for tf in TFS:
351	        rows_ = []
352	        R_ = results["timeframes"][tf]
353	        for p in R_["rules"] + [dict(id="union_all8", untestable=False, L1=R_["union"]["L1"], L0=R_["union"]["L0"], boot=R_["union"]["boot"], holm_p_round=None, maxt_adjusted_p=None, go_no_go=R_["union"]["go_no_go"], blocks=R_["union"]["blocks"])]:
354	            for lab in ("L1", "L0"):
355	                r = dict(id=p["id"], label=lab, ledger_id=p[lab]["id"], untestable=p["untestable"], **{k: p[lab].get(k) for k in keys})
356	                if lab == "L1":
357	                    r.update(holm_p_round=p.get("holm_p_round"), maxt_adjusted_p=p.get("maxt_adjusted_p"), boot_diff_ci=p["boot"]["diff_ci"] if p["boot"] else None,
358	                             go_no_go=p["go_no_go"]["passed"], blocks_positive=p["blocks"]["blocks_positive"], blocks_defined=p["blocks"]["blocks_defined"], half_0_5=p["blocks"]["half_0_5"], half_6_11=p["blocks"]["half_6_11"])
359	                rows_.append(r)
360	        pd.DataFrame(rows_).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, f"round0_scores_{tf}.csv"), index=False)
361	        pd.DataFrame([dict(id=p["id"], **p["blocks"]) for p in R_["rules"]] + [dict(id="union_all8", **R_["union"]["blocks"])]).to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, f"round0_blocks_{tf}.csv"), index=False)
362	    log(f"null_result {results['null_result']}; ledger rows {results['ledger_rows']}; ledger sha {results['ledger_sha_before']} -> {results['ledger_sha_after']}; done in {results['runtime_s']} s")

# H1 gate audit: what the frozen ST7 (1 min) / ST8 (5 min) gates skip vs keep

Study folder `fz_v3/out/studies/h1_gate_audit/`. Scripts `h1_gate_audit.py` (the audit, 138.6 s, log `h1_gate_audit.log` / `run.log`) and
`h1_posthoc.py` (one post-hoc ledger row, 18.2 s, log `h1_posthoc.log`). Every number below is IS only (SETUP date <= 2025-12-31) and
comes from a harness ledger row (id given) or from a CSV in this folder. Ledger sha after the audit `33170f8df9f5d50e`, after the
post-hoc row `1ee15dc04860b284`. All tables: `TABLES.md` (auto-generated), `h1_<tf>_<label>_*.csv`, `h1_summary.json`,
`h1_family_posthoc.json`; machine-readable summary `findings.json`.

## 1. Definitions (fixed before any number was looked at)

| term | definition |
|---|---|
| unit | a harness row: a Foundation SETUP taken under the label's book, `harness.load(tf, label)`; IS rows only (1 min L1 4,452, L0 4,502; 5 min L1 826, L0 832) |
| L1 / L0 | L1 = the 15:25 intraday book (primary); L0 = the engine's uncut trade (robustness) |
| kept | `T.F.fz_traded`: ST7/ST8 held a position on the SETUP, a TAKE or a REENTER whose R5 was the SETUP (post-SETUP; the comparator, never a feature). 745 (1 min) / 325 (5 min) IS rows on both labels |
| gate_at / outcome_gate | `fz_gate` as of the SETUP bar / `fzpost_outcome_gate` (REENTER when a later REENTER used the SETUP as its R5). They differ on 11 IS rows on 1 min (BLOCK -> REENTER, all filled one bar later) and 96 on 5 min (WATCH -> REENTER) |
| block_key | `BLOCK:<fz_block_reason>` when outcome_gate is BLOCK; `WATCH:<fz_block_reason>` when outcome_gate is WATCH and a refused TAKE branch set a reason (`leave_into_recycle`); else the outcome gate. Same definition as the local `h1_common.py`, so the cross-check is like for like |
| loser / winner | label net <= 0 / > 0 (costs included) |
| precision, recall, lift | P(loser given skipped); P(skipped given loser); precision / base loser rate (1.0 = skipping at random). `lift` is derived from the ledger row's `loser_precision` and the IS base loser rate |
| winner recall | count: P(kept given winner); net-weighted: kept winners' net / all winners' net |
| big / huge winner | label pts >= 50 / >= 100 |
| pts bucket | <=-50, (-50,-20], (-20,0], (0,20], (20,50], (50,100], >100 |
| hold bucket | label bars held: 1-5, 6-15, 16-30, 31-60, 61-120, 121-375, >375 (bars on both timeframes; a 5 min bar is five 1 min bars) |
| visit bin | `fz_visit_n`: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4+ / none (no ref room) |
| variants | pre-declared, each a ledger row of family `h1/<variant>`: `frozen` (kept = fz_traded), `take_only` (fz_gate == TAKE), `take_or_reenter_at_setup` (fz_gate in TAKE, REENTER), `not_block` (fzpost_outcome_gate != BLOCK: WATCH rows treated as taken; DIAGNOSTIC, post column), `skip_only:<block_key>` (keep = block_key != key, one row per key; DIAGNOSTIC, the key uses the post outcome gate) |
| post-hoc | `not_block_asof` (fz_gate != BLOCK), declared after the audit's numbers were seen because the SPA best on 1 min / L1 was the post-column `not_block`; counted in the family (`h1_posthoc.py`) |
| FZ book | the ST7/ST8 position's own net on the kept rows (`fzpos_l1_net_inr` under L1, `fzpos_net_inr` under L0), Foundation's label net on the other rows; scored as label `<label>_fzpos` under family `h1/fz_book`. A TAKE is Foundation's own position (identical net on every TAKE row); a REENTER fills a bar later and exits by its own rules (`band_reclaim`) |
| selection-only book | `frozen` on the label itself: Foundation's label net on the kept rows |
| bridge | Foundation IS net + avoided price move of the skipped rows (-sum pts x 65) + avoided costs of the skipped rows (sum `cost_inr` = charges + 2 x 5 pts x 65 slippage) + REENTER exit delta = FZ book net (asserted to close within 0.05 INR on all four tables) |
| group tables | descriptive decompositions of the `frozen` ledger row by as-of and post columns; no rule was chosen on them |

Control percentile = `fz_report.random_control` (2,000 session-matched draws, seeded by the candidate tag): the share of draws whose kept
net is below the candidate's. Permutation p = `fz_report.permutation_p` (kept vs skipped label net, 2,000 shuffles). Because the
control matches per-session position counts while `diff` pools all rows, the two can disagree in sign for a near-complete keep
(e.g. `skip_only:BLOCK:open_pierce`: the 53 skipped rows are better than the pool but worse than the other rows of their own
gap-open sessions). Both are reported; neither alone is the criterion.

## 2. The frozen gate vs the pre-registered comparator

The `h1/frozen` rows reproduce `results/pre_registration.json` (`comparator/frozen_st7_st8`) on every statistic; the control
percentile moves by 0.2-2.1 points because the draws are seeded by candidate tag (1 min L1 64.7 vs 62.6; L0 50.0 vs 49.2; 5 min L1
11.6 vs 13.6; L0 28.1 vs 26.5).
